result.summary: Do not ship yet: reset tokens leak into web responses, file-creation failures escape handling, and the exposed recovery flow cannot complete.

findings.title: Reset tokens are disclosed through the web log viewer
findings.body: The warning goes to both console logging and logging.py:72-84's web buffer. GET /partials/log-viewer renders that buffer at routes.py:1083-1093. Verified that an API-key-authenticated request returns the minted token in HTTP HTML. This newly exposes the operator-only recovery secret to web/API credentials; it is not an unauthenticated disclosure.
findings.recommendation: Send recovery tokens through a dedicated console-only sink, excluding the event from the web buffer, and test the log-viewer response for token absence.

findings.title: Temporary-file creation failures abort the reset request
findings.body: mkstemp runs before the try block. A full or read-only config volume therefore raises through the awaited executor at lines 1698-1700, returning HTTP 500 after the token and rate-limit state have already been committed. Injecting ENOSPC reproduced the unhandled exception, contradicting the intended non-fatal file fallback.
findings.recommendation: Move temporary-file creation inside the protected block and condition cleanup on successful allocation so creation failures still return the neutral confirmation.

findings.title: The newly exposed recovery flow has no token consumer
findings.body: GET /reset/request now exposes a working token-request form and POST mints a token, but the registered router contains only these two reset routes. The confirmation form in templates/reset.html:29 targets /reset/confirm, which returns 404 even with the minted token and matching passwords. Operators can initiate recovery but cannot reset their password.
findings.recommendation: Implement and connect the confirmation page and token-consuming handler before exposing the request flow, or gate the entire flow until recovery works end to end.

next_steps: Fix the three paths and verify token confidentiality, storage-failure fallback, and successful end-to-end password recovery.
